title: Interactive investigation playbook: metric catalog and trace lexicon
body:
Purpose

This doc is a working playbook for making observability maximally useful for interactive investigations (oncall/ops, SE debugging, and pre-rollout checks). Focus: reduce time-to-insight for operator flows by clarifying metric semantics, aligning trace labels, and recommending a small set of investigation-first dashboard widgets and interactions.

Goals
- Create a compact metric catalog prioritized for exploratory debugging (not a full metric census).
- Standardize trace/span annotations and a small lexicon so different teams can stitch session context quickly.
- Propose a dashboard interaction matrix: which widgets to show for rapid triage, what filters/operators matter, and how to surface relevant traces/samples.
- Short runbook snippets for common investigation patterns (latency spikes, cold-cache regressions, model-quality regressions).

Design principles
- Investigation-first: show signals that answer the immediate questions operators ask (who, what, when, how bad, how to reproduce).
- Lightweight: prefer a few high-signal widgets over many noisy panels.
- Cost-aware: prefer sampled traces and aggregated metrics to keep query costs bounded.
- Traceable: every dashboard action should link to trace examples or a prompt replay where possible.

Metric catalog (priority set)
- request.count: Count of inference requests (per-route, per-model, per-tenant). key tags: route, model_version, tenant_id, region.
- latency.p50 / p90 / p99: End-to-end request latency (ms). Tagging as above plus path-stage (ingress, model, postprocess).
- token.emit.count: tokens emitted per request. Useful for cost anomalies and regressions.
- kvcache.hits / misses: prefix/KV cache hit rate (per-model, per-tenant). Denominator: cache.lookups.
- batch.size.avg: average tokens or requests batched per GPU call. Tracks batching efficiency.
- gpu.utilization.avg: GPU utilization percentage per host pool (coarse).
- fallback.rate: fraction of requests routed to fallback model/region.
- error.rate: application-level errors (400/500 family), plus model-failure tags (OOM, kernel-error).
- output.quality.alerts: small counter of automated eval failures from quality probes (per-model).
- cost.perk-token: derived metric for operator view.

Each metric should include: measurement, primary tagset, typical aggregation (rate / quantile / sum / avg), suggested SLI mapping. Keep the catalog intentionally small — this is the operator lean set.

Trace lexicon (span/attribute guidelines)
- session.id: unique per end-user session/request chain. Always present as top-level span tag.
- request.id: unique per transport request (maps to API request header).
- model.call: span for the model inference kernel call. attributes: model.name, model.version, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, quantized=true|false.
- batch.exec: spans that represent GPU batch execution. attributes: batch.size, batch.latency, host.id.
- kv.lookup: span for KV/prefix cache lookup. attributes: cache.key_count, hit=true|false, ttl_bucket.
- router.decision: span when routing/fallback decisions occur. attributes: policy, reason (capacity|latency|region|tier).
- output.filter: span for post-generation structured filtering or safety checks. attributes: filter.type, matched=true|false.
- retry.attempt: span for transient retry logic. attributes: attempt.count, retry.reason.

Sampling guidance
- Adaptive sampling: always keep 100% sampling for error.rate > 0.5% over 5m.
- Session-preserving sampling: when sampling is active, capture full traces for sampled session.ids so follow-on investigations can stitch requests.
- Cost cap: target average trace retention sampling at 1–3% cluster-wide under steady state.

Dashboard interaction matrix (recommended widgets and behaviors)
1) Incident Summary strip (top of dashboard) — 1-row: current SLO breach state, short counts (request.count, error.rate, fallback.rate), time picker quick ranges (5m/1h/24h). Click an error tile -> opens trace sample list filtered to error=true.
2) Latency heatmap (route x quantile) — shows p50/p90/p99 over time. Brush to zoom, the zoom action selects sample traces by highest latency traces (prefers traces with model.call.span present).
3) Request cohort slicer — table + sparkline by tenant_id / model_version / route showing request.count and token.emit.count. Each row links to a quick filter and to a sample trace.
4) Batch efficiency panel — avg batch.size and tokens-per-batch; hovering suggests recommended batch policy changes (tooltip with suggested target).
5) Cache health tile set — kv.lookup hit rate, ttl distribution; clicking low-hit tenant -> runbook suggestion to pre-warm or reduce TTL.
6) Model quality microprobe list — small table with output.quality.alerts + example prompt/response (sanitized). Clicking example opens a prompt replay with trace context.
7) Trace sample rail (right column) — compact list of 5 candidate traces based on the current filter (errors, latency, rare routes). Each trace includes quick actions: copy session.id, open flame graph, start prompt replay.

Operator flows (common tasks)
A) Latency spike triage- Check Incident Summary for affected routes/tenants.
- Use Latency heatmap brush -> open top-N traces -> inspect model.call and batch.exec spans to decide whether spike is model-side or batching-related.
- If model.call shows normal kernel latency but batch.exec latency high, suspect host-level contention. Check gpu.utilization.avg and host error logs.
- If kv.lookup miss spike correlates, consider cold cache warmup.

B) Cold-cache regression- Indicators: kv.lookup.miss increase, token.emit.count stable, latency increase for p90/p99.
- Use cohort slicer to locate heavy-miss tenant.
- Quick mitigation: temporarily increase prefix cache TTL for affected tenant, or route low-priority traffic to warmed pool.

C) Output-quality regression- Indicators: output.quality.alerts and manual reports.
- Use model-quality microprobe to surface representative inputs. Re-run in sandbox with the same model.version and prompts in a reproducible harness (link to PR runner).
- If failure reproduces, create a revert/canary plan and schedule a rollout pause.

Quick SQL/snippet examples (for operators)
- Top tenants by error rate (30m):
SELECT tenant_id, count(1) as requests, sum(case when status >= 500 then 1 else 0 end) as errors
FROM inference_requests
WHERE ts > now()-interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 20;

- Find traces for a request id:
SELECT * FROM traces WHERE tags->>'request.id' = 'REQ-...';

Runbook checklist (investigation starter)
- Reproduce the signal in synthetic probe if possible (link to synthetic-runner).
- Collect 3 representative traces (fastest, median, slowest).
- Sanitize traces (remove PII) and attach to incident ticket.
- If fix requires rollback, ensure 1) canary is prepared, 2) traffic split tested, 3) rollback automation verified.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should session.id be globally unique across all frontends or per-region? (tradeoff: cross-region stitching vs label cardinality).
- How many microprobe examples should be kept per model before we start incurring storage/retention costs? Proposal: 50 per model, rotate by recency + severity.
- Do we need an operator-facing indexer that maps tenant->top-trace-samples by recent anomalies? (would speed triage).

Next steps
- Align with serving-runtime and platform-engineering on the trace lexicon (request: sync 2026-01-25).
- Prototype the Incident Summary strip in the observability sandbox (owner: Diego).
- Add the SQL snippets to the operator quickcards and ship a one-hour workshop for SREs.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Add mapping from each metric to chart templates (saved queries + panel JSON) — follow-up ticket JIRA-OBS-4188.
- Draft small JSON schema for span attributes to enforce via instrumentation lint job.

References
- Confluence: Investigation Playbook (linked).
- Synthetic probe runner repo (github link in linked_artifacts).
